elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: The inserted Performance Warranty warrants only that services "will conform in all material respects to the requirements of this Agreement and the applicable plan" for thirty (30) days; no professional/workmanlike (industry-standard) performance standard appears anywhere in Article XIII.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (a): "for ninety (90) days following delivery, any software delivered by RevMed to Sanofi under this Agreement will conform in all material respects to its documentation." (Deliverables as such are not separately covered, but software-to-documentation conformance is expressly warranted.)

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: The inserted software warranty runs "for ninety (90) days following delivery," not twelve months.
The inserted services warranty runs "for thirty (30) days following performance," short of the 90-day preferred period.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "RevMed shall, at Sanofi's election, repair, replace or re-perform the non-conforming software or services."
"...or refund the amounts paid for them."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 13.4(b): "Each Party and its Affiliates shall comply in all material respects with all Applicable Law ... in the Research, Development, Manufacture and Commercialization of the Products and performance of its obligations under this Agreement," an operative Article XIII compliance obligation binding RevMed (framed as a covenant rather than a warranty).

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code / virus warranty appears in the inserted clause or elsewhere in the rendered Article XIII language.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (a) gives an express software-to-documentation warranty: "for ninety (90) days following delivery, any software delivered by RevMed to Sanofi ... will conform in all material respects to its documentation." Period meets the 90-day floor and survives Section 13.5 because it is expressly stated in Article XIII.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (b): "for thirty (30) days following performance, the Research, Development, Manufacturing and other services performed by RevMed under this Agreement will conform in all material respects to the requirements of this Agreement and the applicable plan."

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "RevMed shall, at Sanofi's election, repair, replace or re-perform the non-conforming software or services."
"...or refund the amounts paid for them" — refund remedy expressly available for the non-conforming software or services.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: 90-day software-to-documentation conformance, 30-day services conformance, repair/replace/re-perform, and refund are all in the inserted operative sentence, and the insertion sits inside Article XIII so the Section 13.5 carve-out ("EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS ARTICLE XIII") preserves it without any edit to the disclaimer — correctly avoiding an unnecessary carve-out redline.

Preferred level fails on four elements: no professional-and-workmanlike standard, software period is 90 days rather than 12 months, services period is 30 days rather than 90 days, and there is no no-malicious-code warranty. If the drafter wants the preferred position, add an express "performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards" clause, extend the periods to twelve (12) months / ninety (90) days, and add a malicious-code warranty.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion, no deletion or paraphrase of retained language (13.1, 13.2, 13.4(b)-(c) and 13.5 are untouched), no survival tail, expense allocation, damages categories, notice procedure or other boilerplate extras. "Re-perform" is a services-appropriate form of the repair/replacement remedy rather than an added requirement. Note that "at Sanofi's election" is more customer-favourable than the model "at Vendor's option"; it is a necessary allocation of the remedy choice and does not add a requirement outside the checklist, but expect Vendor pushback and it can be conceded to "at RevMed's option" without losing any element.

Intent preserved: the express-warranty exception in Section 13.5 makes the new clause consistent with the retained disclaimer; no cross-reference is broken and no undefined term is introduced (the clause self-defines its subject matter as software delivered and services performed under the Agreement).

Practical drafting point (not a defect against the checklist): confirm the insertion is numbered (e.g. Section 13.4A) in the executed redline so that the Section 13.5 "expressly stated in this Article XIII" reference and any later cross-references are unambiguous; the rendered text shows only the heading "Performance Warranty".

In this pharma collaboration the software limb may have little practical work to do; it is retained because the fallback checklist requires an express software-to-documentation warranty, and the services limb tied to "the requirements of this Agreement and the applicable plan" carries the real content.
